chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who forgets while he is behind the Imam, whether to glorify (say Subhana Rabbial-A'la) in prostration or in bowing, or he forgets to say anything between the two prostrations, so he said: 'There is no blame upon him.'

key_terms.خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ: behind the Imam (following in congregational prayer)
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: there is no blame/penalty upon him
key_terms.يُسَبِّحَ: to glorify (referring to saying Subhana Rabbial-A'la)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person forgets to say the glorification in ruku or sujud during prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of *sunnah* glorifications in prayer, establishing that forgetting them incurs no penalty (*la 'alayhi shay'*). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that these specific remembrances are recommended acts of devotion rather than obligatory pillars, offering practical ease for the worshipper. It reflects the broader Shia emphasis on distinguishing between essential components of prayer and the virtuous additions that enhance spiritual presence.
